description: Minimal scientifically valid multi-chain lattice-polymer aggregation model. Extends the validated single-chain ISAW replica-exchange architecture (remd_uniform_chain_2_new.py) to M identical self-avoiding chains in a periodic cubic box, reusing the single-chain fitted contact free energy without refitting. This document is the model/software CONTRACT; it deliberately does NOT hard-code one set of runtime parameters (M, N, L, temperatures, lambda values). Those are chosen per run and recorded in each run's output metadata.

system.number_of_chains_meaning: number of identical, connected self-avoiding chains simulated simultaneously
system.beads_per_chain_meaning: beads per chain (chain length); n_steps = N - 1 covalent bonds per chain
system.box_size_meaning: side length of the periodic cubic lattice box (integer); wrapped lattice sites number L^3
system.excluded_volume: Each wrapped lattice site may contain at most one bead (single occupancy).
system.minimum_box_size_reason: L < 3 creates ambiguous nearest-neighbor wrapping (a bead's +d and -d neighbor sites can coincide); such boxes are rejected.

volume_fraction.meaning: monomer volume fraction: fraction of the L^3 lattice sites occupied by beads. Must satisfy phi <= 1 (M*N <= L^3).

unwrapped.role: AUTHORITATIVE representation for chain connectivity and per-chain geometry (radius of gyration).
unwrapped.notes: Unwrapped coordinates are contiguous along each chain: consecutive bonded beads differ by exactly one lattice step (unit Manhattan distance). A chain may extend beyond [0, L); it is never wrapped for geometry.
unwrapped.canonicalization: After an ACCEPTED move, the moved chain is re-based by an integer multiple of L per axis so its bead 0 lies in the primary box [0, L)^3. This bounds unwrapped magnitudes (preventing whole-chain-translation drift to infinity) while preserving wrapped coordinates, occupancy, site_owner, connectivity, all contact counts, per-chain Rg, and the reduced potential. Canonicalization never runs on trial coordinates before the contact-delta evaluation.

wrapped.role: Derived (coord mod L). Used for occupancy, excluded-volume checks, contact counting, and interchain collision tests.
wrapped.definition: wrapped = ((unwrapped % L) + L) % L, applied component-wise so results lie in [0, L).
wrapped.notes: A chain crossing a periodic boundary must retain the correct Rg after using the unwrapped coordinates; wrapped coordinates are used only for occupancy and contacts.

occupancy.representation: mapping from wrapped lattice site (x, y, z) in [0, L)^3 to a unique global bead ID (NOT merely a set).
occupancy.global_id_inverse: chain_index = global_id // N ; monomer_index = global_id % N

contacts.authoritative_statement: Raw lattice contact counts m_intra and m_inter are AUTHORITATIVE. Every contact is counted exactly once, canonicalized as the unordered global-ID pair (min_id, max_id).

m_intra.definition: number of unique nonbonded nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on the SAME chain (wrapped nearest neighbors), counted once per unordered pair.
m_intra.bonded_exclusion: Covalently bonded nearest neighbors (same chain, |monomer_i - monomer_j| == 1) MUST NOT be counted as intrachain contacts.

m_inter.definition: number of unique nearest-neighbor contacts between beads on DIFFERENT chains (wrapped nearest neighbors), counted once per unordered pair.
m_inter.bonded_exclusion: Not applicable (different chains share no covalent bond); all interchain nearest-neighbor pairs count.

contacts.counting_rule: For every occupied bead, examine its six wrapped nearest-neighbor sites, retrieve any neighboring bead owner, canonicalize the pair as (min_id, max_id) so it is counted exactly once, classify as intra (same chain) or inter (different chains), and exclude covalently bonded same-chain neighbors. Integer counts throughout.

contact_offset.statement: Any molecular-to-lattice contact offset stored in the single-chain fit is excluded from the raw multi-chain contact counts and Hamiltonian.
contact_offset.reason: The offset was fitted for single-chain intrachain contact-number support alignment during free-energy fitting; it must not be applied to interchain contacts or to raw lattice counts used for sampling.

contact_normalization.purpose: Raw m_intra and m_inter are extensive, globally-unique contact-PAIR counts and remain the Hamiltonian variables. Intensive per-chain normalizations (dividing by the number of chains M) are added for ANALYSIS ONLY so runs with different M can be compared. They do not modify sampling, energy, or acceptance.

interpretation.m_inter_pairs_per_chain: globally-unique interchain contact PAIRS divided by M (each interchain contact counted once globally).
interpretation.m_inter_incidences_per_chain: average number of interchain-contact ENDPOINTS (incidences) associated with a chain; each interchain pair contributes one incidence to each of its two participating chains, hence the factor of 2.
interpretation.naming_rule: The two interchain normalizations are named distinctly (pairs vs incidences); neither is called simply 'm_inter_per_chain' because that would be scientifically ambiguous.

contact_normalization.scope: Comparisons across M should use the normalized quantities IN ADDITION to the raw totals. Normalization removes the leading extensive dependence on chain number only; it does NOT remove all finite-size or concentration effects.
contact_normalization.invariance: Normalized contacts, like raw contacts, are never rescaled by rg_scale (they are counts, not lengths).

reduced_potential.equation: u(X, T) = b(T) * [ lambda_intra * m_intra(X) + lambda_inter * m_inter(X) ]
reduced_potential.sampling_weight: P(X | T) proportional to exp(-u(X, T))

b_of_T.meaning: reduced contact bias b(T) for the selected contact-bias model, loaded with the SAME semantics as remd_uniform_chain_2_new.py (MODEL_REGISTRY, fitted params, Tref, Tscale).
b_of_T.loading: Loaded through the existing fit_summary.json and model-registry interfaces (resolve_model_params / load_fit_summary_json). Fitted parameters are never modified or refit.
b_of_T.single_chain_consistency: For M = 1 and lambda_intra = 1, u reduces to b(T) * m_intra, matching the single-chain reduced potential u = m * b(T).

effective_energy.label: temperature-dependent EFFECTIVE energy (reported for compatibility only; the reduced potential u is the canonical sampling quantity). It is NOT a temperature-independent microscopic energy.

lambda_intra.meaning: coupling multiplier on intrachain contacts in the reduced potential

lambda_inter.meaning: coupling multiplier on interchain contacts in the reduced potential

lambda_controls.note: lambda_intra and lambda_inter select control modes WITHOUT changing the energy implementation.

full_transferability.meaning: null model: a monomer-monomer contact has the same effective free energy whether intra- or interchain (DEFAULT).

independent_collapse.meaning: chains collapse independently; interchain contacts do not affect acceptance.

interchain_attraction_only.meaning: only interchain contacts contribute; intrachain contacts do not affect acceptance.

athermal_control.meaning: no contact energy; all valid configurations have equal reduced potential.

replica_exchange.swap_rule: log_accept = u(X_i, T_i) + u(X_j, T_j) - u(X_j, T_i) - u(X_i, T_j)
replica_exchange.swap_rule_note: Generalized reduced-potential swap rule. Because u depends on both m_intra and m_inter (and on lambda_intra, lambda_inter), swap calculations MUST use BOTH cached contact counts, not the total contact count alone.
replica_exchange.temperatures: Temperatures are fixed to lanes; complete MultiChainState objects are exchanged between adjacent lanes with even/odd alternation.

local_sweep.definition: 1 local sweep = M * N local move proposals

translation_sweep.definition: 1 translation sweep = M whole-chain translation proposals

sweep_conventions.interface: The run is parameterized by local_sweeps_per_swap and translation_sweeps_per_swap (NOT a single ambiguous absolute steps_per_swap). Both the sweep counts and the actual per-cycle proposal counts are recorded in output metadata.

local.name: end
local.description: move one selected-chain end bead to a random empty neighbor of its anchor bead

local.name: crankshaft
local.description: local corner/kink flip of one interior selected-chain bead about the axis through its two neighbors

local.name: pivot
local.description: rotate a selected-chain tail about a randomly chosen pivot bead using a proper cubic lattice rotation

collective.name: chain_translation
collective.description: translate every bead of one selected chain by one of the six lattice unit vectors; symmetric proposal; own current sites ignored during the interchain collision test; intrachain contacts are exactly preserved and only interchain contacts involving the translated chain are recomputed

invariants: preserve linear connectivity (unit bonds in unwrapped coordinates)
preserve interchain excluded volume via global wrapped occupancy
null proposals (identical to current state) are not counted as state-changing acceptances

contact_updates.debug_path: Recompute full_contact_counts for every geometrically valid trial state (exact oracle).
contact_updates.production_path: Local delta-contact algorithm: enumerate incident canonical contact pairs before the move, build/update a temporary occupancy for the trial, enumerate incident pairs after, canonicalize IDs, determine removed/added intra/inter contacts (deduplicated when multiple moved beads share a contact), and update cached counts.
contact_updates.translation_optimization: Whole-chain translation cannot change intrachain contacts; only interchain contacts involving the translated chain are recomputed.
contact_updates.debug_assertion: An environment-controlled assertion (MULTICHAIN_DEBUG_CONTACTS, analogous to ISAW_DEBUG_CONTACTS) compares cached counts against full_contact_counts after every accepted move.

per_cycle_records: std of per-chain Rg across chains
optional full per-chain Rg vector in diagnostic output
per_chain_geometry.rg_scale_note: rg_scale is applied only to OUTPUT length quantities, never to sampling. Fields suffixed _lattice are raw lattice lengths; the same field without _lattice equals rg_scale times the lattice value (rg_scale**2 for squared lengths). The std of per-chain Rg follows this rule: std_chain_rg_lattice_post is unscaled, std_chain_rg_post = rg_scale * std_chain_rg_lattice_post; init_mean_chain_rg_lattice is unscaled, init_mean_chain_rg = rg_scale * init_mean_chain_rg_lattice.

chain_cluster_graph.edge_rule: connect two chains when they share at least cluster_contact_threshold interchain contacts
records: largest cluster fraction f_max = s_max / M
chain_cluster_graph.note: This is an explicit chain-level graph built from interchain contact pairs; it is NOT the single-chain bead-level contact-graph S_max.

distribution_semantics.P_mean_chain_rg: cycle-level distribution of the MEAN per-chain Rg across chains.
distribution_semantics.P_chain_rg: distribution of POOLED individual-chain Rg samples (all chains, all post-burn-in cycles); resolves homogeneous collapse vs mixed expanded/collapsed chains. Semantically distinct from P_mean_chain_rg.

diagnostics.central_observables_note: Warnings are raised on the raw extensive central observables only; the per-chain normalized series are deterministic transforms and would raise duplicate warnings.

snapshot_format.coordinate_dtype_note: Production snapshots default to int32. The writer allocates the coordinate dtype once from the first snapshot and cannot widen it later, so it never auto-selects int16; int16 remains available only for explicit, size-bounded use. Coordinate canonicalization keeps unwrapped magnitudes bounded so int32 does not overflow.
snapshot_format.note: The single-chain HDF5 schema (T, bead, xyz) is NOT reused for multi-chain coordinates; chain identity is explicit.

initialization.independent_walkers: Each REMD temperature lane begins from its OWN independently generated dispersed state, using deterministic per-lane seeds init_seed = seed + INITIALIZATION_SEED_STRIDE * lane (stride 1000003, distinct from the per-cycle sweep-seed strides). Initialization occurs in the main process so serial and multiprocessing runs share identical starting states.

scope_notes: This is the minimum scientifically valid multi-chain simulator to test whether the single-chain contact free energy predicts aggregation.
No PNIPAM-specific extensions beyond the transferability null model are introduced.
Cluster translations, cluster rotations, configurational-bias regrowth, and kinetic acceleration moves are out of scope for this stage.
Reptation is optional and not required for initial completion.
